9. Mr. Mahmudul Islam learned Advocate does not support the grounds on which the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. His main contention is that the pre-emption case cannot succeed because of defect of parties as ''rid by the trial court and wrongly rejected by the appellate court. He further submits that the High Court Division did not at all consider this vital issue on the question of defect of parties although that was the first ground before the High Court Division. His main contention is that the miscellaneous case should be dismissed only on the ground of defect of parties. The learned Subordinate Judge found that some of the S.A. recorded tenants have not been made parties and brushed aside, for want of proof, the contention of the appellant that those recorded tenants have no subsisting interest in the holding in question. This objection as to non-joinder of co-sharers was specifically raised in the written objection and inspite of that objection some of the co-sharers have not been impleaded which is legally fatal for the maintainability of the pre-emption petition. 

 10. He further submits that the legal consequence of non-impleading of the admitted co-sharers in the Khatian is a vital omission for which the pre-emption application is not maintainable. 

 12. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate placed before us the case of Akhtarun Nessa and another Vs. Habibullah and ors reported in 31 DLR (AD)-88 and the case of Abdus Samad & ors Vs. Md. Sohrab Ali and others reported in 33 DLR (AD)-113, wherein it is found that the co-sharers having not been impleaded in the application of pre-emption the application is not legally maintainable. As a matter of fact, some of the S.A. recorded tenants as appeared from the khatian filed in this case have been omitted. In view of the legal position the application for pre-emption was not legally maintainable for non-impleading necessary parties in the pre-emption proceeding. Consequently, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.
